rules: When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPP bit is set to 0 if the trap originated from user mode.
When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPP bit is set to 1 if the trap originated from a privilege mode other than user mode.
When an SRET instruction is executed, if the SPP bit was 0, the hart privilege level is set to user mode.
When an SRET instruction is executed, if the SPP bit was 1, the hart privilege level is set to supervisor mode.
When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPP bit is set to 0.
When the SIE bit is clear, interrupts are not taken while the hart is in supervisor mode.
When the hart is in user mode, supervisor-level interrupts are enabled regardless of the SIE bit value.
When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SPIE bit is set to the value of the SIE bit.
When a trap is taken into supervisor mode, the SIE bit is set to 0.
When an SRET instruction is executed, the SIE bit is set to the value of the SPIE bit.
When an SRET instruction is executed, the SPIE bit is set to 1.
When the MXR bit is 0, a load from a page marked only executable (X=1, R=0) fails.
When the MXR bit is 1, a load from a page marked either readable (R=1) or executable (X=1) succeeds.
The MXR bit has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
When the SUM bit is 0, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) fault.
When the SUM bit is 1, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) are permitted.
The SUM bit has no effect when page-based virtual memory is not in effect.
The SUM bit has no effect when the hart is in user mode.
When satp.MODE is read-only 0, the SUM bit is read-only 0.
When the UBE bit is 0, explicit load and store memory accesses in U-mode are little-endian.
When the UBE bit is 1, explicit load and store memory accesses in U-mode are big-endian.
The UBE bit has no effect on instruction fetches.
The UBE bit has no effect on implicit accesses to supervisor-level memory management data structures.
When the SDT bit is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write, the SIE bit is cleared to 0.
An explicit CSR write that sets the SIE bit to 1 is permitted only if the SDT bit is 0 or is being set to 0 by the same write.
When a trap is taken into S-mode, if the SDT bit is 0, it is set to 1.
When a trap is taken into S-mode and the SDT bit is 1, a double-trap exception is delivered into M-mode.
When a double-trap exception is delivered into M-mode due to an unexpected trap into S-mode, the mcause register is set to 16.
An SRET instruction sets the SDT bit to 0.
